title: Azure Key Vault and Secrets Management
description: Learn how to store secrets, keys, and certificates securely using Azure Key Vault and managed identities.

data.text: **Azure Key Vault** is a cloud service for securely storing and accessing secrets. A secret is anything you want to tightly control access to, such as API keys, passwords, certificates, or cryptographic keys.

items: **Secrets** — Opaque values like passwords, connection strings, and API keys.
**Keys** — Cryptographic keys (RSA, EC) used for encryption and signing. Managed through Azure Key Vault's built-in HSM (Hardware Security Module).
**Certificates** — X.509 certificates for TLS/SSL, authentication, or code signing. Key Vault can create, import, and auto-renew them.
**Managed Identities** — An identity for Azure resources (like a VM or App Service) so you never need to store credentials in code.

terms.definition: An automatically managed identity in Entra ID for Azure resources. Eliminates the need for credentials in your code.
A Key Vault feature that retains deleted secrets for 90 days, protecting against accidental or malicious deletion.
A cryptographic key stored in FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or 3 validated hardware for maximum security.

data.text: You can create a Key Vault, add a secret, and retrieve it using the Azure CLI. The example below also shows how to enable a managed identity for an app service.

data.title: Create a Key Vault and store a secret
data.content: These commands create a resource group, a Key Vault, set a secret, and enable a managed identity on an App Service.
data.code:
# Create a resource group
az group create --name rg-security --location eastus

# Create a Key Vault
az keyvault create \
  --name myAppKeyVault \
  --resource-group rg-security \
  --location eastus \
  --enable-purge-protection true

# Store a secret
az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name myAppKeyVault \
  --name "DbConnectionString" \
  --value "Server=tcp:myserver.database.windows.net;..."

# Retrieve the secret
az keyvault secret show \
  --vault-name myAppKeyVault \
  --name "DbConnectionString" \
  --query value -o tsv

data.title: Never Hardcode Secrets
data.text: Key Vault exists so your application never reads secrets from appsettings.json or environment variables that are checked into source control. Always retrieve secrets at runtime using a managed identity.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Key Vault centralizes secrets, keys, and certificates in one encrypted service
Soft-delete and purge-protection guard against data loss
Managed identities remove the need to store credentials in code
Use Azure RBAC or Key Vault access policies to control who can read or write
data.takeaway: Key Vault turns scattered, risky credentials into one auditable, encrypted store — and managed identities mean your code never touches a secret string.
